_readme: ONE object per bookmaker. Everything else is generated from this file:
Workflow: join an affiliate programme -> put the real tracking link in
`affiliate_url`, fill the facts, set `placeholder` to false.
While `placeholder` is true the site shows a visible 'demo entry' badge so
nothing fake is ever presented to readers as a real recommendation.

bookmakers.name: BetHub
pros: Consistently sharp football prices — margins around 2.5% on top leagues
Withdrawals processed the same day on e-wallets
Live streaming included with a funded account
cons: Bonus is not available in every country
Live chat is slower at weekends
bookmakers.verdict: The strongest all-round option in our testing: pricing is competitive enough for regular bettors, payouts are fast, and the app is stable during big fixtures. The welcome offer carries fair 5x wagering, which is well below the market average.

bookmakers.name: PrimeBet
pros: Best welcome offer we tested — just 1x wagering on the free bets
Very deep market coverage, including lower divisions
Local payment methods in India and Nigeria
cons: Curaçao licence offers weaker player protection than MGA/UKGC
bookmakers.verdict: Worth an account purely for the free-bet offer, which is one of the few on the market with realistic terms. Market depth is excellent; the trade-off is a lighter regulatory framework than our top pick.

bookmakers.name: OddsX
pros: Largest headline bonus percentage of the sites we rate
Strong prices on accumulators and outrights
cons: 8x wagering makes the bonus harder to clear than it looks
No iOS app — mobile web only for iPhone users
Withdrawals can take two working days
bookmakers.verdict: A good fit if you bet accumulators and want a large starting balance, provided you read the 8x wagering carefully. iPhone users should note there is no native app.
